newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.05 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.05 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.05 percent to close at 1.0381 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0380 to 1.0430 per dollar, dealers said.
The previous mini-band was set on Dec 16 between 1.0375 and 1.0425 reais to the dollar.
Many dealers were surprised by the Central Bank's move, but the market remained calm on the change.
Dealers said Wednesday's large surplus of $451 million helped calm the market.
In late afternoon the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0380 per greenback to drain the excess dollars from the market.
Dealers also said they continued expecting a total 0.6 percent drop in the real-dollar mini-band in December. So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.55 percent.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.02 percent to end at 1.0434 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.130 per greenback, traders said.
